newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: World churches body condemns U.S. over Cuba law.
newsitem.headline: World churches body condemns U.S. over Cuba law.

text.p: The World Council of Churches (WCC) on Wednesday condemned the United States for launching "a new act of economic aggression" against Cuba with a new U.S. law aimed at foreign investment in the communist island.
A resolution passed by the WCC's 156-member Central Committee said the escalation in U.S. economic sanctions would have "a terrible impact" on the people of Cuba.

The WCC noted that it had regularly joined with churches and ecumenical bodies in Cuba, Latin America, the Caribbean and the United States itself in denouncing earlier economic measures against Havana.

The resolution called on U.S. President Bill Clinton not to apply the measures called for in the new law, the so-called Helms-Burton act, which allows U.S. citizens, including Cuban exiles, to sue foreign companies which use property confiscated after Fidel Castro's 1959 revolution.

Under provisions of the law -- which has been fiercely criticised by all the main U.S. trading partners including the European Union, Canada, Japan and Latin American countries -- Washington has already barred some executives of foreign companies and their families from the United States.
The WCC, which links over 400 million Christians in over 100 countries, also called on the U.S. and Cuban governments "to resolve their differences through negotiation and dialogue."
